correctness.rationale: All matching faces of the explicitly defined graph are enumerated, giving 20,135,365,360,87. Signed simplicial boundaries satisfy d²=0. Modular ranks (19,116,249,87) over 2,3,101 imply those same rational ranks because augmentation and consecutive-composition inequalities provide equal upper bounds, proving only reduced degree-three rational homology of dimension 24. The ten vertex automorphisms preserve all edges and give signed trace vectors (20,135,365,360,87), (0,0,0,0,2), and (2,-3,-5,0,1) for identity/nontrivial rotations/reflections. The reduced Lefschetz identity produces homology traces 24,-1,0. Two rational regular D5 modules and the rational fifth-cyclotomic module have exactly this character; Maschke semisimplicity and finite-group transfer prove the decomposition and orbit-space rank. Every critical computation is supplied as standalone exact executable and checked against its output.

value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is the canonical smallest triangle-free four-chromatic graph; its full D5 symmetry is an intrinsic topological action on a standard matching complex. The known homology rank 24 does not identify either its two regular summands or the four-dimensional cyclotomic rational constituent. The full symmetry module yields the previously unspecified nonzero two-dimensional invariant part and third rational Betti number of its dihedral quotient. A complete natural group-module invariant of this graph is substantive beyond ordinary matching counts or homology ranks; no arbitrary parameter choice is involved.
